proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(m=n_1\) and \(\ell=\log(en)\).  If \(m=0\), the restriction
\(mu\geq C\ell\) is empty, while the definitions give
\(q_t^L=0\leq q_t\leq1=q_t^U\).  Hence take \(m\geq1\).

For \(t\in\{0,1\}\), \(s\in[-1/2,1/2]\), and \(h\in H_n\), put
\[
 C_{t,s,h}=\{z\in A_t:\|z-(0,s)\|_2\leq h\}.
\]
On fixed points \(z_1,\ldots,z_N\), write \(z_i=(r_i,s_i)\).  For fixed
\(t,h\), membership of \(z_i\) in \(C_{t,s,h}\), as a function of \(s\),
is the indicator of the closed interval
\[
 \left[s_i-\sqrt{h^2-r_i^2},
       s_i+\sqrt{h^2-r_i^2}\right]
\]
when \(z_i\in A_t\) and \(|r_i|\leq h\), and is identically zero otherwise.
Thus the trace changes only at at most \(2N\) endpoints.  Since
\(|H_n|\leq 2+\log_2 n\), the number of traces of
\[
 \mathcal C_n=\{C_{t,s,h}:t\in\{0,1\},
 s\in[-1/2,1/2],\ h\in H_n\}
\]
on \(N\) points is at most
\[
 2|H_n|(2N+1)\leq C_0(N+1)\ell.                 \tag{1}
\]

We record the relative-deviation calculation.  For a Bernoulli variable
\(Z\) of mean \(p\), the inequalities
\(e^v-1-v\leq v^2/[2(1-|v|/3)]\), \(|v|<3\), and exponential Markov give
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{|\widehat p-p|>
 2\sqrt{\frac{3p\ell}{m}}+\frac{6\ell}{m}\right\}
 \leq2e^{-6\ell}                                      \tag{2}
\]
for a fixed set.  Introduce an independent sample of size \(m\), apply (2)
conditionally to the pooled \(2m\) observations, and sum over their traces.
Equation (1) bounds the number of pooled traces by \(C_0(2m+1)\ell\).
A second application of (2) to the ghost empirical probability removes the
conditioning.  Enlarging a numerical constant only gives
\[
 \Pr\!\left\{\exists C\in\mathcal C_n:
 |P(C)-\widehat P_m(C)|
 >
 \sqrt{\frac{12\widehat P_m(C)\ell}{m}}
 +\frac{20\ell}{m}\right\}\leq C_1n^{-3}.        \tag{3}
\]
For completeness, if \(d=|P(C)-\widehat P_m(C)|\), then
\(\sqrt{P(C)}\leq\sqrt{\widehat P_m(C)}+\sqrt d\).
Substitution into the population-variance version of (2), followed by
\(2ab\leq a^2+b^2\), absorbs one half of \(d\) into the left side and
leaves the two displayed constants in (3).  Closed endpoints were retained,
so this calculation also covers traces attained at a breakpoint.

Let \(\mathcal E_{1n}\) be the event in (3).  By
\(\widehat P_m(C_{t,s,h})=\widehat q_t^{(1)}((0,s),h)\), (3) and the
definition of \(b_n\) give, simultaneously in \(x,t,h\),
\[
 q_t^L(x,h)\leq q_t(x,h)\leq q_t^U(x,h),\qquad
 a^L(x,h)\leq a_P(x,h)\leq a^U(x,h).             \tag{4}
\]
If \(m q_t(x,h)\geq C_2\ell\), the same algebra, with \(C_2\) large enough,
gives
\[
 \frac12q_t(x,h)\leq q_t^L(x,h)
 \leq q_t(x,h)\leq q_t^U(x,h)\leq2q_t(x,h).       \tag{5}
\]
Apply (5) to a side attaining the minimum and (4) to the other side to get
the asserted constant-factor comparison for \(a^L,a^U,a_P\).

We next establish the same-radius representative property, including every
tie case.  Fix \(h\).  Before duplicate removal, each sample breakpoint is
source-labeled by its coordinate, index, and sign.  Lexicographic sorting
totally orders all labels; if several labels have the same coordinate,
retaining the least label removes only duplicate labels and retains that
coordinate.  Thus every distinct breakpoint is still in \(C_1(h)\).
The deterministic mesh is a set, so a mesh point tied with a breakpoint
also occurs once in the sorted union.  At a breakpoint \(s\), choose
\(g_h((0,s))=(0,s)\); because all empirical balls are closed, this preserves
the entire vector of endpoint memberships, including coincident left and
right endpoints.  At either endpoint of \(B\), make the same choice.
If \(s\) is any other coordinate in the sorted union, again choose it
itself.  Otherwise there is a unique pair of consecutive union coordinates
\(w_j<s<w_{j+1}\); choose their midpoint.  No sample breakpoint lies in
\((w_j,w_{j+1})\), so every empirical membership indicator is constant on
that open interval.  Since \(M_h=\lceil16/h\rceil\), consecutive
deterministic mesh points are \(1/M_h\leq h/16\) apart.  Consequently
\[
 \|g_h(x)-x\|_2
 \leq \frac{1}{2M_h}
 \leq\frac h{32}<\frac h4,\qquad
 \widehat q_t^{(1)}(g_h(x),h)
 =\widehat q_t^{(1)}(x,h),\quad t=0,1.            \tag{6}
\]
This proves the required deterministic representative map for all
breakpoint and mesh ties.

Let \(F\) be an \(h\)-separated subset of
\(\{x:a_P(x,h)\leq u\}\), and for each \(x\in F\) choose a side \(t_x\)
with \(q_{t_x}(x,h)\leq u\).  On \(\mathcal E_{1n}\), (3) and (6) imply
\[
 a^U(g_h(x),h)
 \leq C_3\{u+\ell/m\}.                             \tag{7}
\]
For distinct \(x,x'\in F\), (6) and the triangle inequality give
\[
 \|g_h(x)-g_h(x')\|_2
 \geq h-\frac h{32}-\frac h{32}
 =\frac{15h}{16}>\frac h2.
\]
Upward dyadic rounding multiplies a positive argument by at most two,
except below the smallest positive grid value, where it adds at most
\((m\vee1)^{-1}\), already absorbed by \(\ell/m\).  Taking the constant
\(c\) at least \(2C_3\), (7) and the definition of \(\widehat J\) prove
\[
 J_P(h,u)\leq
 \widehat J\!\left(h,c\{u+\ell/m\}\right).         \tag{8}
\]
The definition accepts every nonnegative second argument and caps it at one
before rounding, so (8) is well typed also at \(u=1\).

Conversely, every qualifying point \(g\) in the finite maximum defining
\(\widehat J(h,v)\) satisfies, by (4) and the dyadic rounding bound,
\[
 a_P(g,h)\leq a^U(g,h)\leq
 \min\{1,C_4(v+\ell/m)\}.                          \tag{9}
\]
Order any nonempty \(h/2\)-separated qualifying set along \(B\), and split
it into odd- and even-indexed points.  Each part is \(h\)-separated.
It is therefore also \(h/8\)-separated, and monotonicity of ball mass in
the radius makes every point thin at radius \(h/8\) at the level in (9).
Each part has cardinality at most
\(J_P(h/8,C_4(v+\ell/m))\).  If the finite maximum is empty, its maximum is
zero but the outer floor makes \(\widehat J=1\).  Combining these two cases,
and substituting \(v=c\{u+\ell/m\}\), yields
\[
 \widehat J\!\left(h,c\{u+\ell/m\}\right)
 \leq
 C_5\left\{1\vee
 J_P\!\left(h/8,C_5\{u+\ell/m\}\right)\right\}.    \tag{10}
\]
Equations (8) and (10) prove the corrected packing comparison.

All maps used above are Borel.  The square-root breakpoint is continuous on
its closed domain; inclusion of a candidate is Borel; sorting a finite
source-labeled list and retaining the least label use finitely many Borel
comparisons.  Deterministic refinement, midpoint formation, and maximization
over subsets of a finite ordered set are likewise Borel.

It remains to bound the exceptional terms used by the estimator.  Apply
(3) also to the independent second half.  Choose \(h^\circ\in H_n\) with
\[
 n^{-1/(4\bar\kappa)}\leq h^\circ
 <2n^{-1/(4\bar\kappa)}.
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), this grid point exists.  The base-mass
assumption, \(n_2\asymp n\), \(h^\circ\leq1\), and
\(\kappa\leq\bar\kappa\) give
\[
 n_2a_P(x,h^\circ)\geq
 c\,n(h^\circ)^{\bar\kappa}\geq c n^{3/4}
 \quad\text{uniformly in }x.                      \tag{11}
\]
Equations (4)--(5), the deterministic segment-packing bound
\(J_P(h,u)\leq1+1/h\), and (10) show that \(h^\circ\) is admissible for
every \(x\), for all sufficiently large \(n\).  The unit floor in (10)
changes the logarithm by at most a numerical constant.  Hence the selected
criterion is no larger than
\[
 d_n=C\left\{
 Ln^{-1/(4\bar\kappa)}
 +\sigma n^{-3/8}\sqrt{\ell}\right\}.              \tag{12}
\]
Its variance term and admissibility consequently imply
\[
 \inf_x n_2a_P(x,\widehat h(x))
 \geq c\,d_n^{-2}\geq c n^{1/(2\bar\kappa)}.       \tag{13}
\]
The second-half version of (3), or (2) followed by the trace count (1),
and then a union bound over the finitely many score traces, gives
\[
 \Pr\{\exists x,t:N_t^{(2)}(x,\widehat h(x))=0\}
 \leq Cn^{-3}.                                     \tag{14}
\]
Equation (11) also rules out an empty admissible-bandwidth set on the
relative-deviation event.  Enlarging \(C\) handles the finitely many smaller
\(n\).  Thus the event probability in the theorem is at most
\(C\ell^2/n\).  Projection bounds the contrast loss by \(4L\), so the
exceptional expected contribution is at most
\(C(L+\sigma)\ell^2/n\).

Finally, on \(\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa\), put
\(b=n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\), up to a factor-two dyadic adjustment, and write
\(a_P(x,b)=wb^\kappa\).  The base-mass assumption gives \(w\geq c_m\), and
the isolated-envelope assumption gives
\[
 J_P(b,\min\{1,Ca_P(x,b)\})
 \leq C\{1+w^{1/(\kappa-2)}\}.                    \tag{15}
\]
When the threshold is clipped at one, this follows from the envelope at
\(u=1\) and \(w\geq C^{-1}b^{-\kappa}\).  Since
\[
 \sup_{\substack{\kappa\in K\\w\geq c_m}}
 \frac{
 1+\log\!\left(e\{1\vee w^{1/(\kappa-2)}\}\right)}
 {w}<\infty,
\]
the severity-layer contribution at (15) is \(O(b)\), while the exceptional
term is \(o(b)\), uniformly on \(K\).  The correction \(J_P\mapsto1\vee J_P\)
only contributes the constant \(\log e=1\); it cannot introduce a leading
\(\log n\) factor.  This proves the final assertion.

The construction uses only finitely many Borel operations on \(I_1\) at
each \(h\in H_n\).  The preceding lemma proves measurability of
\(C_1,G_1,\widehat J,a^L,a^U\).  A minimum over the finite ordered set
\(H_n\), with the stipulated smallest-minimizer rule, is Borel.  The
second-half counts and sums are finite Borel sums, their zero-count branch is
explicit, and both projections are continuous.  Hence
\(\widehat\tau_n\) is a total Borel map.  Its formula contains neither
\(\kappa\) nor a class label.

Put \(\ell=\log(en)\), and, with the numerical constant \(C_0\) supplied
by the packing comparison, define
\[
 V_P(x,h)=Lh+\sigma
 \sqrt{\frac{
 1+\log\!\left(
 e\left\{1\vee
 J_P\!\left(h,\min\{1,C_0a_P(x,h)\}\right)\right\}\right)}
 {na_P(x,h)}}.                                    \tag{16}
\]
The base-mass assumption gives \(a_P(x,h)\geq c_mh^\kappa>0\), so every
denominator in (16) is positive and every logarithm is defined.  Let
\[
 \mathcal R_P=\sup_{x\in B}\inf_{h\in H_n}V_P(x,h).
\]
On the first-half event \(\mathcal E_{1n}\) from the preceding lemma,
positivity of \(a^L(x,h)\) implies
\((n_1\vee1)a_P(x,h)\geq c\ell\): positivity means
\(\widehat q_t^{(1)}>b_n(\widehat q_t^{(1)})\) on both sides, and the
relative-deviation inequality (3) of that lemma gives the claim.  Thus its
(5), (8), and corrected (10), applied also at the rounded level
\(\widehat u(x,h)\), show that every admissible empirical criterion
\[
 \widehat V(x,h)=Lh+4\sigma
 \sqrt{\frac{1+\log(e\widehat J(h,\widehat u(x,h)))}
 {n_2a^L(x,h)}}
\]
obeys
\[
 C_1^{-1}V_P(x,h)
 \leq\widehat V(x,h)
 \leq C_1V_P(x,h)+C_1\sigma\frac{\ell^2}{n}.       \tag{17}
\]
Indeed, when the comparison profile is empty, corrected (10) replaces it by
one, exactly as in (16); this changes \(1+\log(\cdot)\) by a numerical
constant and not by \(\ell\).  The additive term in (17) covers the bottom
dyadic severity cell.

If an \(h\) attaining the finite infimum in (16) is not empirically
admissible, the first-half relative-deviation bound and (8) imply
\(V_P(x,h)\geq c\sigma\).  The projected loss is at most \(4L\), which is
bounded by \(CV_P(x,h)\), with \(C\) allowed to depend on the fixed ratio
\(L/\sigma\).  Otherwise minimization and (17) give
\[
 \widehat V(x,\widehat h(x))
 \leq C\inf_{h\in H_n}V_P(x,h)
      +C\sigma\frac{\ell^2}{n}.                   \tag{18}
\]
Thus (18) holds in the risk bound in both cases; an empty admissible set is
retained in the explicit exceptional event.

We now establish the stochastic step.  Conditional on all scores and on
\(I_1\), write
\[
 \varepsilon_i
 =Y_i-T_im_{1,P}(X_i)-(1-T_i)m_{0,P}(X_i),
 \qquad i\in I_2.
\]
The conditional sub-Gaussian assumption and independent sampling give, for
every deterministic \(A\subseteq I_2\),
\[
 E_P\!\left[
 \exp\!\left\{\lambda\sum_{i\in A}\varepsilon_i\right\}
 \,\middle|\,X_1,\ldots,X_n,I_1\right]
 \leq\exp\!\left(\frac{\sigma^2\lambda^2|A|}{2}\right).   \tag{19}
\]
Exponential Markov and minimization over \(\lambda\) therefore give
\[
 P\!\left\{\left|\sum_{i\in A}\varepsilon_i\right|
 >\sigma\sqrt{2|A|z}\,\middle|\,X_1,\ldots,X_n,I_1\right\}
 \leq2e^{-z}.                                      \tag{20}
\]

For the flat profile peeling, fix a side and bandwidth, order centers along
\(B\), and partition them by dyadic cells of their population side mass.
A maximal \(h\)-separated subset of a nonempty cell with upper mass \(u\)
has at most \(J_P(h,u)\) points, because
\(\{x:q_t(x,h)\leq u\}\subseteq\{x:a_P(x,h)\leq u\}\).
Every remaining center is within \(h\) of one of these points.  Within that
interval, each score contributes to the ball sum on one interval of centers,
as shown in (1) of the preceding lemma.  Successive bisection at its
endpoints and (19) give
\[
 P\!\left[
 \sup_{\substack{x:q_t(x,h)\leq u\\
                  q_t(x,h)>u/2}}
 \frac{\left|\sum_{i\in I_2}
 \varepsilon_i\mathbf1\{X_i\in A_t,\|X_i-x\|_2\leq h\}\right|}
 {N_t^{(2)}(x,h)\vee1}
 >
 C\sigma\sqrt{\frac{
 1+\log\!\left(e\{1\vee J_P(h,u)\}\right)+z}
 {n_2u}}
 \right]\leq2e^{-z}.                              \tag{21}
\]
To verify the bisection bound, expose the at most \(2N\) interval endpoints
one at a time.  At level \(r\), at most
\(2^r\{1\vee J_P(h,u)\}\) partial sums occur, while their unexplained
conditional variance is at most \(2^{-r}n_2u\sigma^2\).  Apply (20) with
\(z+\log(e\{1\vee J_P(h,u)\})+2r\), and sum
\(\sum_{r\geq0}e^{-2r}\).  The event
\(N_t^{(2)}<n_2q_t/2\) is bounded by the same calculation with centered
Bernoulli indicators and is absorbed by increasing \(C\).

Apply (21) successively at
\[
 u_j=\min\{1,2^j a_P(x,\widehat h(x))\},\qquad j=0,1,\ldots,
\]
stopping when \(u_j=1\).  The numerator scale grows as \(2^{j/2}\), whereas
division by the count contributes \(2^{-j}\).  The resulting expectations
are bounded by
\[
 C\sigma\sqrt{
 \frac{1+\log\!\left(
 e\left\{1\vee J_P\!\left(
 \widehat h(x),
 \min\{1,C_0a_P(x,\widehat h(x))\}\right)\right\}\right)}
 {n_2a_P(x,\widehat h(x))}}
 \sum_{j\geq0}2^{-j/2}.                            \tag{22}
\]
There is no factor equal to the number of severity cells.  If selected
bandwidths differ, perform the same bisection after ordering the selected
intervals by decreasing radius.  An interval not contained in a previously
charged interval contributes an \(h\)-separated center to the appropriate
packing; a contained interval is charged to the next bisection level of its
ancestor.  Every interval is charged once, and at charge depth \(r\) its
variance is at most \(2^{-r}\) times its ancestor's variance.  Thus the same
geometric series controls all \(h\in H_n\).  Integrating (21) in \(z\), using
\(\int_0^\infty e^{-z}\,dz=1\), gives
\[
 E_P\!\left[
 \sup_{\substack{x\in B,\ t\in\{0,1\}\\
 N_t^{(2)}(x,\widehat h(x))>0}}
 \left|
 \frac{\sum_{i\in I_2}\varepsilon_i
 \mathbf1\{X_i\in A_t,\|X_i-x\|_2\leq\widehat h(x)\}}
 {N_t^{(2)}(x,\widehat h(x))}
 \right|
 \,\middle|\, I_1\right]
 \leq
 C\sup_{x\in B}\{V_P(x,\widehat h(x))-L\widehat h(x)\}
 +C\sigma\frac{\ell^2}{n}.                        \tag{23}
\]
The bottom severity cell and the complement of the two relative-deviation
events contribute the last term, by the preceding lemma, (19), and
integration of (20).  The protected unit floor contributes only a numerical
constant at every severity level, so the summation remains the geometric
series in (22), not a global \(\log n\) factor.

For a positive second-half count, causal-mean Lipschitzness gives
\[
 \left|
 \frac{\sum_{i\in I_2}m_{t,P}(X_i)
 \mathbf1\{X_i\in A_t,\|X_i-x\|_2\leq h\}}
 {N_t^{(2)}(x,h)}
 -\theta_{t,P}(x)\right|\leq Lh.                  \tag{24}
\]
The trace-envelope assumption gives
\(\theta_{t,P}(x)\in[-L,L]\), so projection onto \([-L,L]\) cannot increase
the error in (24).  Projection onto \([-2L,2L]\) likewise cannot increase
contrast error.  Sum (24) over the two sides, combine (18) and (23), and use
the \(4L\) loss bound on a zero-count or empty-admissible-set sample.  This
yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 &\leq C\mathcal R_P+C\sigma\frac{\ell^2}{n}\\
 &\quad+4L\,P\!\left\{\exists x\in B:
 \min_tN_t^{(2)}(x,\widehat h(x))=0
 \mathbin{\text{or}}
 \nexists h\in H_n,\quad
 n_2a^L(x,h)\geq
 64[1+\log\{e\widehat J(h,\widehat u(x,h))\}]
 \right\}.
\end{aligned}                                      \tag{25}
\]
By (16), this is the proposed displayed oracle inequality.  Equations
(11)--(14) of the preceding lemma bound its event probability by
\(C\ell^2/n\), uniformly over \(\kappa\in K\).  The two remainder terms are
therefore at most \(C(L+\sigma)\ell^2/n\), completing the proof.

The construction of \(\widehat\tau_n\) contains neither \(\kappa\) nor the
names \(\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa,\mathrm{Perv}_\kappa\); it remains to evaluate
the proved oracle inequality for the two classes.

Fix \(\kappa\in K\).  For the isolated class, let
\(b=n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\), and choose \(h_b\in H_n\) with
\(b\leq h_b<2b\), which is possible for all sufficiently large \(n\).
Write
\[
 a_P(x,h_b)=w_xh_b^\kappa.
\]
The base-mass assumption gives \(w_x\geq c_m\).  Choose the numerical
constant in the theorem so that \(C_0c_m\geq C_m\).  With
\(\alpha=\kappa-2\), the isolated-envelope assumption gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 J_P(h_b,\min\{1,C_0a_P(x,h_b)\})
 &\leq C_{\mathrm{iso}}\left\{
 1+h_b^{-1}
 \left(\frac{C_0w_xh_b^\kappa}{h_b^2}\right)^{1/\alpha}
 \right\}\\
 &\leq C\{1+w_x^{1/\alpha}\}.                     \tag{26}
\end{aligned}
\]
If the threshold is clipped at one, the envelope at \(u=1\) and
\(w_x\geq C_0^{-1}h_b^{-\kappa}\) give the same inequality.  Since
\(\epsilon\leq\alpha\leq\bar\kappa-2\),
\[
 \sup_{\alpha\in[\epsilon,\bar\kappa-2]}
 \sup_{w\geq c_m}
 \frac{
 1+\log\!\left(e\{1\vee C(1+w^{1/\alpha})\}\right)}
 {w}<\infty.                                      \tag{27}
\]
Also \(nh_b^\kappa\asymp h_b^{-2}\).  Substitution of (26)--(27) into
(16) of the theorem yields, uniformly in \(x,P,\kappa\),
\[
 V_P(x,h_b)
 \leq CLh_b+C\sigma
 \sqrt{\frac{
 1+\log\!\left(e\{1\vee C(1+w_x^{1/\alpha})\}\right)}
 {nh_b^\kappa w_x}}
 \leq Cb.                                         \tag{28}
\]
The protected floor is bounded by the already present constant in
\(C(1+w_x^{1/\alpha})\), so it adds no \(\log n\).  Moreover
\(\log^2(en)/n=o(b)\) uniformly on the compact exponent window.  The theorem
and (28) prove
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa}
 E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \leq Cn^{-1/(\kappa+2)}.                         \tag{29}
\]

For the pervasive endpoint, in fact for every
\(P\in\mathrm{Base}_\kappa\), every \(h\)-separated subset of the unit-length
segment \(B\) has at most \(1+1/h\leq2/h\) elements because \(h\leq h_0\leq
1/8\).  Hence
\[
 1\vee J_P(h,u)\leq2/h                            \tag{30}
\]
for every \(u\geq0\).  Let
\(r=(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\), and choose
\(h_r\in H_n\) with \(r\leq h_r<2r\).  By base mass, (30), and
\(\log(e/h_r)\leq C\log n\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \sup_{x\in B}V_P(x,h_r)
 &\leq CLh_r+
 C\sigma\sqrt{\frac{\log(e/h_r)}
 {nc_mh_r^\kappa}}\\
 &\leq C(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.                \tag{31}
\end{aligned}
\]
Again the theorem's remainder is smaller uniformly on \(K\).  Since
\(\mathrm{Perv}_\kappa\subseteq\mathrm{Base}_\kappa\), (31) gives
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathrm{Perv}_\kappa}
 E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 \leq C(\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}.                 \tag{32}
\]
The same total estimator appears in (29) and (32), proving simultaneous
endpoint adaptation.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
There are constants \(c,C\) and events \(\mathcal E_n\) with
\(\inf_{P\in\bigcup_{\kappa\in K}\mathrm{Base}_\kappa}P(\mathcal E_n)
\geq1-Cn^{-3}\) such that, simultaneously for \(h\in H_n\) and
\(u\in U_n\) satisfying \(n_1u\geq C\log(en)\),
\[
 J_P(h,u)\leq
 \widehat J\!\left(h,c\{u+\log(en)/n_1\}\right)
 \leq
 C\left\{1\vee
 J_P\!\left(h/8,C\{u+\log(en)/n_1\}\right)\right\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal E_n\), \(a^L(x,h)\leq a_P(x,h)\leq a^U(x,h)\) for every
\(x,h\), and the bounds are within constant factors when
\(n_1a_P(x,h)\geq C\log(en)\).  For every \(h\in H_n\), the source-labeled
lexicographic sorting, duplicate removal, and midpoint map defining
\(C_1(h)\) and \(G_1(h)\) are Borel functions of \((X_i)_{i\in I_1}\);
the finite maximum defining \(\widehat J(h,u)\) is therefore Borel for every
\(u\in U_n\).  The confidence calibration, zero-count event, and
\(h_0\)-fallback event together contribute at most
\(C(L+\sigma)\log^2(en)/n\) to expected supremum risk and introduce no
leading global \(\log n\) factor on \(\mathrm{Iso}_\kappa\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The empirical packing count is defined with a floor at \(1\), while the population packing number is \(0\) for an empty thin set.  The unprotected upper comparison is therefore false in that case; retaining \(1\vee J_P\) is the exact correction and leaves all nonempty-profile rates unchanged.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
The total estimator \(\widehat\tau_n\) is Borel measurable, is defined on
zero-count samples and empty admissible-bandwidth sets, and uses neither
\(\kappa\) nor the profile class.  There is a finite constant \(C\), uniform
over \(K\), such that for every \(\kappa\in K\) and
\(P\in\mathrm{Base}_\kappa\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E_P\|\widehat\tau_n-\tau_P\|_\infty
 &\leq C\sup_{x\in B}\inf_{h\in H_n}
 \left\{
 Lh+\sigma\sqrt{
 \frac{
 1+\log\!\left(
 e\left\{1\vee
 J_P\!\left(h,\min\{1,Ca_P(x,h)\}\right)\right\}\right)}
 {n a_P(x,h)}}
 \right\}
 +C\sigma\frac{\log^2(en)}n\\
 &\quad+
 4L\,P\!\left\{\exists x\in B:
 \min_{t\in\{0,1\}}N^{(2)}_t(x,\widehat h(x))=0
 \quad\mathbin{\text{or}}\quad
 \nexists h\in H_n,\quad
 n_2a^L(x,h)\geq
 64\left[1+\log\{e\widehat J(h,\widehat u(x,h))\}\right]
 \right\}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Moreover the displayed event probability is at most \(C\log^2(en)/n\), so
the last two terms are bounded by
\(C(L+\sigma)\log^2(en)/n\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The oracle logarithm must inherit the corrected unit floor from the empirical-packing comparison.  Replacing \(J_P\) by \(1\vee J_P\) makes the functional defined even when the relevant population thin set is empty and adds only a numerical constant, not a global \(\log n\) term.

prose_updates.tldr: A single total measurable split-sample estimator adapts to the unknown multiplicity of polynomially thin sites along an identified causal boundary trace.  A deterministic source-labeled arrangement, tie-safe mesh refinement, and upper-confidence packing count produce the first-half penalty, while zero-defined and envelope-clipped second-half side averages produce the trace estimate.  The empirical upper comparison retains its unavoidable \(1\vee J_P\) floor, and the population oracle logarithm uses the same protection.  This costs only a numerical constant and no leading global \(\log n\).  The resulting oracle inequality yields, for the same estimator, the isolated rate \(n^{-1/(\kappa+2)}\) and pervasive rate \((\log n/n)^{1/(\kappa+2)}\); the endpoint minimax benchmarks and normalized witnesses remain attributed to the banked parent result.

project_justification.gap: Degenerate-design theory treats one point or finitely many one-dimensional zeros, while boundary-curve theory assumes density bounded away from zero.  Neither gives a total unweighted-supremum estimator that measurably learns thin-site multiplicity while remaining valid when a queried population thin set is empty.
project_justification.niche: The missing object is a profile-adaptive estimator whose stochastic penalty is the protected packing entropy \(1+\log\{e(1\vee J_P)\}\) at each site's local mass severity, with every sample-dependent selection and every breakpoint tie defined on every realization.
project_justification.fill: The project constructs an explicit source-labeled first-half arrangement, proves that deterministic mesh refinement preserves every empirical pattern within distance strictly below \(h/4\), estimates the corresponding floored packing entropy, uses zero-defined clipped second-half side averages, proves a population oracle inequality with an event-explicit negligible remainder, and derives both endpoint rates from one procedure without a hidden global logarithm.

prose_updates.honest_scope: The profile-adaptive packing-oracle inequality is the sole closed novelty claim.  Identification, the measurable empirical-packing comparison, and flat-law validity support that theorem.  Because \(\widehat J\geq1\) by construction whereas an empty population thin set has \(J_P=0\), the valid upper comparison and oracle entropy use \(1\vee J_P\); this protection adds only a numerical constant and does not alter either endpoint rate.  The estimator is total: empty side counts map to zero before clipping, an empty admissible set maps to \(h_0\), and the final contrast is clipped to \([-2L,2L]\).  The endpoint minimax orders belong to the banked \(\texttt{stat\_bdd\_thickness\_estimability\_frontier}\) result; the corollary here claims only simultaneous upper-rate attainment by one estimator.  At \(\kappa=3\), the retained witness divergence is \(nL^2h^5/(480\sigma^2)\).  Formally setting \(\kappa=2\) in the balances recovers the bivariate Lipschitz pointwise rate \(n^{-1/4}\) and uniform rate \((\log n/n)^{1/4}\), without uniform constants at that excluded endpoint.

statement_notes.justification: This proof-critical component supplies a tie-safe measurable selector and the corrected floored packing comparison needed to prevent both an undefined empty-profile logarithm and a hidden global logarithm in Theorem 1.
statement_notes.gap: Design-adaptive regression does not supply the measurable severity-layer packing comparison needed for this boundary oracle theorem; the lemma is supporting rather than a second headline claim.
statement_notes.consumer: It certifies that the implementable penalty distinguishes localized support holes from pervasive scarcity, including the case of an empty population thin set, without measurability gaps.

statement_notes.justification: The protected packing-oracle inequality is the sole closed novelty claim and makes local thin-site multiplicity, with the necessary unit floor for empty profiles, rather than global boundary cardinality determine the stochastic penalty.
statement_notes.gap: Gaiffas (2007) gives pointwise adaptation and Gaiffas (2009) gives spatial normalization for finitely many zeros; neither gives this measurable unweighted boundary-supremum profile oracle with a total empty-profile-safe penalty.
statement_notes.consumer: Practitioners obtain a fully defined density-free causal-curve estimator without knowing the depletion exponent or regime; the unit floor changes only a numerical constant.

statement_notes.gap: The banked result supplies separate endpoint procedures and minimax benchmarks, but not one total \(\kappa\)-free and profile-free estimator attaining both endpoint upper rates.
